who.what: a child keeping a nature notebook

wants.what: to fill a page with the things found outdoors

because.what: the finds turn up one at a time, and the page stays half empty for a long while

becomes.what: the page fills with specimens and gets its name, 博物笔记

memory.detail: sticking a beetle and a butterfly side by side on a squared notebook page and writing a title under them

leave: Old public domain plates can make a new page.

device.what: cut-out specimens that fall onto the page like stickers, each with a paper sound as it lands
device.why: sticking finds onto a page is how a field notebook fills up

change.from: an empty cream page with a faint square grid, a beetle cut-out falling onto it
change.to: the Hercules beetle and a birdwing butterfly stuck side by side

change.from: two specimens on the page, a third falling in
change.to: four specimens in a row: the beetle, the butterfly, a flower chafer and a cone shell

change.from: the full board with nothing written on it
change.to: 博物笔记 written under the row of specimens

change.from: the board titled 博物笔记
change.to: Field notes from the public domain in brown under the title, the view a little closer
